title: Quantum Codes from $r$-Nearly Self-Orthogonal Linear Codes via Jordan Canonical Form over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$
authors: Liangdong Lu, Ruipan Yang, Yang Liu, Qiang Fu, Guanmin Guo
abstract: We introduce a Jordan-canonical-form framework for constructing $q$-ary quantum stabilizer codes from arbitrary classical linear codes over $\F_{q^2}$. The framework does not require the classical linear code $\mathcal{C}$ to satisfy the dual-containing condition (i.e., self-orthogonality). Given a classical code $\mathcal{C}=[n,k,d]_{q^2}$ with parity-check matrix $H$, we measure the obstruction to Hermitian self-orthogonality by the rank $r=(n-k)-\dim_{\F_{q^2}}(\mathcal{C}^{\perp_h}\cap \mathcal{C})$. The ingredient code $\mathcal{C}$ is $r$-nearly dual containing, or, equivalently, $\mathcal{C}^{\perp_h}$ is $r$-nearly self-orthogonal, by which we mean that $r=\Rank(HH^{\dagger})=\dim_{\F_{q^2}}(\mathcal{C}^{\perp_h})-\dim_{\F_{q^2}}(\mathcal{C}^{\perp_h}\cap \mathcal{C})$. By systematically reducing the rank of the Hermitian inner-product matrix $A=HH^{\dagger}$ through rank-one perturbations along the Jordan basis $W=P^{-1}$ of the decomposition $A=PJ_AP^{-1}$, we construct an explicit Hermitian self-orthogonal code $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{so}}=[n+r,n-k]_{q^2}$. A sufficient distance-preservation criterion guarantees that the resulting $q$-ary quantum code has parameters $[[n+r,2k-n+r,\geq d]]_q$. Applying this construction to classical codes produces several record quantum codes that improve or supplement the best-known parameters in Grassl's tables.
summary: This paper presents a novel Jordan-canonical-form framework for constructing $q$-ary quantum stabilizer codes. It allows the construction to proceed from any classical linear code by quantifying its deviation from self-orthogonality using rank reduction ($r$). This systematic approach yields explicit, record-breaking quantum codes with improved parameters.
main_problem: The primary goal is to construct $q$-ary quantum stabilizer codes from arbitrary classical linear codes over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$, circumventing the restrictive requirement that the classical code must be Hermitian self-orthogonal.
main_result: The authors introduce a Jordan-canonical-form framework that systematically constructs an explicit Hermitian self-orthogonal code $C_{so}$ and, consequently, a quantum code with parameters $[[n+r, 2k-n+r, \geq d]]_q$.
method: The method involves measuring the obstruction to Hermitian self-orthogonality using the rank $r$ of the matrix $HH^\dagger$, followed by iteratively reducing this rank via rank-one perturbations along the Jordan basis.
model_or_system: The model is Quantum Error-Correcting Codes (QECCs) realized through the stabilizer formalism, which are mathematically mapped to classical linear codes over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ equipped with a Hermitian inner product.
key_observables: Quantum code parameters $[[n+r, 2k-n+r, \geq d]]_q$, and the rank $r = 	ext{Rank}(HH^\dagger)$.
important_parameters: The field size $q$ (and $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$), code parameters $[n, k, d]_{q^2}$, and the rank reduction parameter $r$.
main_assumptions: The construction relies on the existence of the Jordan canonical form for Hermitian matrices over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ and a distance-preservation criterion based on this decomposition.
figures_summary: The notes reference TABLE VI, which lists numerous calculated quantum codes derived from cyclic codes using the Jordan extension method, detailing parameters like $r$ and the defining set $\mathbf{w}$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by noting the limitations of existing constructions; it then introduces the Jordan-canonical-form framework to quantify the deficiency ($r$) and systematically construct a self-orthogonal code via rank reduction theorems, culminating in explicit examples.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful algebraic tool (Jordan form) to bridge classical coding theory with quantum error correction, offering systematic methods to generate high-performance codes without requiring overly restrictive initial conditions on the underlying classical structure.
